content.overview: The share capital of a Producer Company shall consist of equity shares only. The shares held by a Member in a Producer Company shall, as far as may be, be in proportion to the patronage of that company.
content.glance: Equity shares only; Member shareholding linked, as far as may be, to patronage.
content.study: Section 378ZB establishes two capital-structure rules for Producer Companies. First, the share capital may consist only of equity shares; preference shares are not permitted. Second, a Member’s shareholding should, as far as may be, reflect that Member’s patronage of the company. The ‘as far as may be’ formulation is not an absolute mathematical requirement but a guiding principle linking use of the company’s services to shareholding.

sections.heading: Rule
sections.body: Share capital consists of equity shares only; Member shareholding shall, as far as may be, be in proportion to patronage.

examples.title: Illustration — s. 378ZB
examples.body: A Producer Company issues only equity shares and allocates additional shares to Members in line with their greater use of the company’s marketing services, consistent with the patronage principle in s. 378ZB(2).

hypotheticals.question: What is the core effect of s. 378ZB?
hypotheticals.analysis: It confines Producer Company capital to equity shares and links shareholding, as far as may be, to patronage.

rows.right: Special user rights or transfer of shares (later sections)

misconceptions.trap: Assuming preference shares may be issued by a Producer Company.
misconceptions.correction: s. 378ZB(1) requires that the share capital consist of equity shares only.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should s. 378ZB be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. State equity-only capital. II. Apply the patronage-proportion principle. III. Conclude.
